raised.claim: Verdicts attached to a newly proposed issue are never checked against that issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a proposal has scope `{ beer_ids: [2], where: [] }` but beer 1 references its key, beer 1 is accepted, the issue is created, and its DB row is linked even though the issue's own scope rejects beer 1; the same attachment would be refused once the issue already existed.

raised.claim: Any nonempty `beer_ids` list bypasses the prohibition on a `where` made only of `review_class`.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope such as `{beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}]}` is accepted as legal, but `rowSatisfiesScope` uses OR semantics, so every future `matcher_bug` verdict satisfies the class term and the issue again becomes a whole-class dumping ground.

raised.claim: The absence guard accepts one empty probe even when the other probe returned evidence that the beer exists.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a probe like `{ brewery: '', name: 'Other Brewery — Target Beer' }`, `proved` is true and a `not_on_untappd` verdict remains terminal, despite the name probe finding the beer and the prompt explicitly treating a beer found under a different brewery as a brewery-label problem; only the contradictory result is retained.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not account for other attachments planned in the same run.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue has 11 post-creation rows and two current verdicts target it, both see the unchanged value 11 and are accepted, resulting in 13 rows despite `MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE = 12`; an empty issue can similarly receive an entire batch at once.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: The trusted scope block is appended after model-authored body text, allowing an earlier model-authored `triage-scope` fence to override it when the first block is parsed later.
raised.why_it_breaks: If `issue.body` contains a valid ` ```triage-scope ` block, the completed issue has that block before the rendered structured scope; `parseScopeBlock` uses the first regex match, so the next run silently trusts the model-body scope instead of the validated scope that was appended by the job.

raised.claim: Guard counters are logged only when the model omitted batch IDs, not when guards actually reject submitted verdicts.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a one-row batch where the model supplies one verdict that violates the target scope, `covered` equals the batch size while `plan.guardHits.scope_violation` is 1, so no shortfall warning is emitted and the rejected row can recur silently—the exact loop the new counters are intended to expose.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Reopening a row after its candidate-count category changes clears its review fields but leaves the new authoritative `issue_number` link intact.
raised.why_it_breaks: A row previously attached to issue 347 that changes from zero to nonzero candidates becomes untriaged with `review_class`, `review_note`, and `reviewed_at` set to NULL, but still reports `issue_number = 347`, leaving the new authoritative relationship inconsistent until a later triage happens to overwrite it.

raised.claim: Quiet `matcher_bug` verdicts introduced by the new absence degradation path are counted as `wontfix` in the persisted outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: When an unsupported `not_on_untappd` verdict is degraded to `matcher_bug`, it is placed in `plan.quiet`; this loop takes the `else` branch and increments `outcome.wontfix`, so the daily triage digest reports a wontfix that was never recorded as such.

raised.claim: The saturation count is not monotonic because it counts only issue-linked rows still present in `enrich_failures`.
raised.why_it_breaks: After 12 rows have been attached to an issue, matching and clearing one of those failures deletes it from `enrich_failures`; the query then returns 11 and permits another attachment, allowing an issue to accumulate more than 12 post-creation attachments over time despite the stated cap.

raised.claim: The migration backfill extracts the first `→ #` occurrence rather than the issue suffix appended by triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a legacy note whose model-authored text already contains an issue reference, such as `related to → #123; alias gap → #347`, `instr` starts at `#123` and backfills issue 123 instead of the actual attached issue 347, corrupting the row-to-issue link and saturation counts.
